title: Understanding Cross-Validation
text: Cross-validation is a technique used to assess how the results of a statistical analysis will generalize to an independent data set. It is mainly used in settings where the goal is prediction, and one wants to estimate how accurately a predictive model will perform in practice.

title: Bias and Variance in Cross-Validation
text: Increasing the number of folds in k-fold cross-validation can affect the bias and variance of the model. Think about how using more folds might change the amount of data used for training versus testing in each iteration.

title: Evaluating Cross-Validation Efficiency
text: Consider the computational cost of cross-validation compared to regular validation. Does cross-validation require more or less computation?

title: Training Data Utilization
text: One advantage of cross-validation is that it allows the model to be trained and tested on different subsets of the data. This means that every data point gets to be in a test set exactly once and gets to be in a training set k-1 times.

title: Cross-Validation in Production
text: Think about whether cross-validation is typically used during the model development phase or in production. Does it involve using the entire dataset for training and testing?
